title: Top-Up — an expired smartcard is topped up and reactivated
preface: This test is to confirm an expired smartcard product can be topped up and returned to a valid state.
preconds:
**GIVEN** an Operator at the top-up screen with an expired smartcard presented
**AND** an example expired Adult iLink smartcard

steps.expected:
**THEN** the smartcard is returned to a valid state
**AND** a top-up receipt is printed

expected:
An expired smartcard is reactivated by a top-up and a receipt printed.
Data variations: product {iLink, BVP, Metro Travelcard, Daylink}; passenger {Adult, Child}

title: Ticket Issue — an advance-dated ticket
preface: This test is to confirm an Operator can apply an advance date to an eligible ticket type for future travel.
preconds:
**GIVEN** an Operator on the ticket-sales screen with an advance-dateable ticket type selected
**AND** an example future travel date within the configured advance-date period

steps.content: **WHEN** the Operator applies the advance date and takes payment
steps.expected: **THEN** the ticket is printed carrying the future travel date

expected:
An advance-dated ticket is issued printed with its future travel date.
Data variations: mode {NIR-Rail, Glider}; passenger {Adult, Child}

preface: This test is to confirm a Multi-Journey top-up that would exceed the configured maximum journey count is prevented.
preconds:
**GIVEN** an Operator topping up a Multi-Journey smartcard already close to the configured maximum journey count
**AND** the tester knows the currently configured maximum (50 journeys per prior test evidence) and an example top-up that would exceed it

steps.content: **WHEN** the Operator views the printed ticket and receipt
steps.expected:
**THEN** only a masked PAN is shown
**AND** the full card number is not printed

title: Supervisor — override/end an operator break (ID entry and card)
preface: This test is to confirm a Supervisor can override/end an operator's break, signing the operator off, either by entering their ID or by presenting their card.
preconds:
**GIVEN** an operator is in break mode on the HHD
**AND** the seeded Supervisor ID and PIN, and a valid Supervisor card, are available
**AND** worked example: a Supervisor overriding a break on the G1 Glider route (Metro)

steps.content: **WHEN** the supervisor overrides the break by entering their ID and PIN
steps.expected:
**THEN** the operator break is ended
**AND** the operator is signed off, without the operator's PIN

steps.content: **WHEN** the supervisor instead overrides the break by presenting their card
steps.expected:
**THEN** the operator break is ended
**AND** the operator is signed off, without the operator's PIN

expected: A Supervisor can override/end an operator break by ID+PIN entry or by presenting their card, signing the operator off without needing the operator's PIN.

preconds:
**GIVEN** an Operator is signed on to the HHD
**AND** an available HHD printer is in range to be paired
**AND** worked example: an Operator pairing the printer at the start of a Glider (Metro) shift
**GAP** — REQ-0819.6 confirms the HHD carries its own integrated 2\" thermal printer (not a separate paired accessory); REQ-0819.8 documents the HHD's Bluetooth/NFC short-range wireless as being for pairing to an *external payment card device* only. No source confirms an HHD-to-printer Bluetooth pairing workflow exists; likely conflated with the M020 payment-device pairing (C4104007) or invented — confirm on the live system before running

**GIVEN** a Technician is signed on to the HHD with an HHD printer available
**AND** worked example: a Technician connecting a printer during commissioning
**GAP** — REQ-0819.6 confirms the HHD's printer is integrated hardware, not a separate pairable accessory; REQ-0819.8's Bluetooth/NFC capability is documented only for pairing an external payment card device (the M020), not a printer. The MAC-entry-vs-barcode-scan connection workflow this case describes is not documented anywhere; likely conflated with M020 pairing or invented — confirm on the live system before running
